thesisQuality.note: Q2 Energy Storage sales rose 78% and volume 11%, while Kemerton idling shows resource scale does not ensure durable conversion economics.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q2 sales rose 31% and adjusted EBITDA increased materially with about $3.2B liquidity, while earnings remain lithium-price sensitive.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Sep. 30 market valuation and cycle-distorted earnings imply balanced rather than clearly cheap asymmetry.

catalystScore.note: Kings Mountain institutional support and Q2 price/volume recovery are credible catalysts, with timing and commodity durability uncertain.

governancePower.note: Cost actions, capex restraint and debt reduction show adaptive allocation, offset by CEO-transition uncertainty.

alignment2036.note: Lithium chemicals serve batteries, mobility and grid storage while Kings Mountain supports domestic critical-mineral supply; independent industry research supports long-run storage demand but constrains near-term certainty.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Energy Storage is complemented by Specialties across semiconductor, oil/gas, flame-retardant and pharmaceutical markets, though lithium remains dominant.

bottleneckControl.note: Large lithium resource/conversion footprint provides meaningful constraint participation, but Kemerton idling disproves unassailable bottleneck control.

scenarioRobustness.note: Liquidity, cost actions and Specialties diversification help, but EBITDA outcomes remain highly lithium-price sensitive and independent research shows near-term stationary-storage demand can decline with policy changes.

substitutionResilience.note: Qualified lithium materials and resource positions create moderate barriers, while alternative producers and conversion-cost pressure remain credible.

supplyChainResilience.note: Global mining/conversion interests and Kings Mountain diversify supply, while Kemerton idling and physical-ramp dependencies remain material.

pricingPower.note: Q2 Energy Storage realized price rose materially, but lithium pricing remains largely market-driven.

risk.note: Commodity-price sensitivity, conversion economics, physical ramp disruption, leadership transition and policy-sensitive storage-demand paths remain material risks.

confidence.note: Recent issuer results, government project records, independent governance reporting, current market data and independent industry demand research provide source-diverse coverage; realized lithium pricing, restart economics and the 2026 storage-demand trajectory remain uncertain.

thesis: Albemarle combines strategically important lithium resources, improving operating momentum and a stronger balance sheet with long-duration battery relevance, constrained by commodity, conversion and demand-path uncertainty.
keyRisk: Lithium-price weakness, structurally uncompetitive conversion economics or policy-sensitive demand can overwhelm volume growth.
nextCatalyst: Next earnings and operating update plus leadership-transition execution.
